source.stem:
Which of the following options regarding Darwin’s theory of natural selection is incorrect ( )
A. All living things generally have strong reproductive capabilities
B. If living things want to survive, they must fight for survival in order to obtain food and space.
C. Variations produced by organisms must be conducive to adapting to the environment
D. Organisms that do not adapt to the environment will be eliminated

options.text: All living things generally have strong reproductive capabilities
If living things want to survive, they have to fight for food and space.
Variations produced by organisms must be conducive to adapting to the environment
Creatures that do not adapt to the environment will be eliminated

hinge.title: Decide whether respectful interaction and responsible social media behaviour are part of a balanced social life during adolescence.
node_labels: Living systems: organisms, health and ecosystems

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Sharing a classmate's accurate personal information without their permission is responsible online behaviour.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: A friendly online group guarantees that its members' posts are responsible.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Spreading false rumours online does not count against a balanced social life because it is not face-to-face.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: A false rumour written politely with friendly emojis is respectful online behaviour.

intelligence.enrichment: A balanced social life requires polite and respectful interaction with others. During adolescence, new experiences and emotions make it important to be thoughtful and responsible in person and on social media, including avoiding harmful online actions such as misleading messages, false rumours, and sharing personal information without consent. thoughtful and respectful behaviour -> favourable social environment; irresponsible digital behaviour -> cyberbullying harms others The learner applies respectful interaction and responsible online behaviour as parts of a balanced social life during adolescence. Online behaviour is not part of real social life, so posts and rumours do not need the same respect as face-to-face interaction.
